about: Cortex-A57 in the Tegra X1 (Switch). sim: a57sim.c parameters; cost: cost.py prices. role fit = set from the calibration point named; src = where the number comes from. CC = Chips and Cheese, 'Cortex A57, Nintendo Switch's CPU' (2023-12-12, measured on a Switch under Linux at 1.785 GHz); 7CPU = 7-cpu.com/cpu/Cortex-A57.html (Opteron A1170, 2 GHz); TRM = ARM Cortex-A57 TRM r1p3; E = estimate.

l1i_kb: CC, TRM (the brief's 32 KB I is the A53's)
l2_kb: CC (Tegra X1 chose the 2 MB option)
page_shift: E: 4 KB pages, as on Linux; Horizon may map the heap with larger blocks (fewer TLB misses)
ind_bits: ARM slides via CC: 512 indirect targets
window: E: ~40 bundles in flight (CC) at ~1.5 instructions per bundle
pf_l1: TRM: L1D stride prefetcher, on by default
pf_l2_lines: CC: up to 8 prefetches after an L2 miss, inside the 4 KB page
stream_l1: TRM: write streaming after consecutive line writes (threshold E)
sb_window: E: instructions a store stays in the store buffer

dram_ns: fit chase_64m: CC ~250 cycles at 1.785 GHz, with the TLB walks of a 64 MB chase on 4 KB pages
tlb1_pen: CC: the L2 TLB adds over 20 cycles
walk_pen: E: a page walk whose descriptors hit L2
btb_l2_bubble: CC: taken branch 1 cycle from the L1 BTB, 2 from the L2 BTB
ic_l2_pen: CC: code from L2 at ~1 IPC, i.e. ~16 cycles per 16-instruction line instead of ~5
l2_bytes_per_cycle: CC: ~8 B/cycle from L2 for one core
dram_mlp_lines: fit memcpy_nano (tinymembench 3504 MB/s at 1.43 GHz); CC: the A57 L2 has 20 pending fills
indep_tlb_factor: E: a TLB miss of an independent load overlaps half its latency
